sources.entry: akshare - A financial data interface library, with data provided for academic research only.

summary.one_liner: AKShare is a Python library that fetches Chinese and international financial market data (stocks, bonds, futures, funds, macro indicators and more) from public data websites in a few lines of code, intended for academic research.
summary.what_it_does: AKShare provides a set of Python functions, each wrapping a data interface, that return financial data as pandas DataFrames. The README's examples show fetching daily A-share historical prices for a stock with a single call and plotting US stock candlesticks with mplfinance. It includes an offline interface registry with keyword search (ak.search) and a lookup function (ak.interface_info) that returns parameters, output columns and a usage example for a named interface. Data is sourced from many websites named in the acknowledgements, including Eastmoney, Sina Finance, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges, and several futures exchanges. The README also mentions AKTools as an HTTP API for use from other programming languages. Documentation is in Chinese and covers installation, tutorials, a data dictionary and indicators.
use_cases: fetch historical A-share stock prices in Python
download financial data for academic research
look up which function returns a given market dataset
pull futures, bond or fund market quotes
plot candlestick charts of US stock prices
feed financial data to LLM-driven programs via keyword interface search
access Chinese financial data from Python without an HTTP API
how_to_run: stock_zh_a_hist_df = ak.stock_zh_a_hist(symbol="000001", period="daily", start_date="20170301", end_date="20231022", adjust="")
pip install mplfinance  # optional, for the plotting example
stack: AKTools (HTTP API, separate project mentioned in README)
notable: Offline interface registry with keyword search (ak.search) and per-interface metadata lookup (ak.interface_info), designed for LLM-driven programs
Covers a wide range of Chinese financial data sources including major stock, futures and bond exchanges and Eastmoney/Sina Finance
Optional HTTP API (AKTools) for use from languages other than Python
Documentation in Chinese with tutorials, data dictionary and indicator guides
caveats: README states all data is for academic research only and not investment advice
Some data interfaces may be removed due to uncontrollable factors, per the statement section
